note: An experiment (GAME_SPEC §13.7, Stage 43) on data/benches/dilution.json: what pH measures. 1 M sulfuric acid diluted tenfold three times, the pH climbing about a unit each time (a little less: the ions' activity coefficients rise as the solution thins).
title: Experiment: diluting an acid

steps.part: A tenth, a hundredth, a thousandth
steps.title: 5 mL of acid into 45 mL of water
steps.text: Pick up the acid bottle, then right-click the first beaker. Drag the menu's slider to about 5 mL, then click "pour". Point at the beaker: the readout shows its pH.
steps.why: The bottle holds 1 M sulfuric acid. pH counts the hydrogen ions in powers of ten: pH 1 is a tenth of a mole of them in a litre, pH 2 a hundredth. Each H2SO4 gives two of them.

checks.text: about 50 mL in the first beaker

steps.title: A tenth of that
steps.text: Pick up the first beaker, then right-click the second. Slide to 5 mL (a tenth of it) and pour.
steps.why: Ten times less acid in the same volume: ten times fewer hydrogen ions, so the pH goes up by about one.

checks.text: about 50 mL in the second beaker

steps.title: A monitor on the last beaker
steps.text: Drag a monitor out of the parts drawer onto a free square. Drag from its sensing port onto the third beaker. Click "vessel", then "pH".
steps.why: The third beaker holds only water now: pH 7, neutral, as many hydroxide ions as hydrogen ions.

checks.text: a monitor reads the third beaker's pH

steps.title: Below pH 4
steps.text: Click "below". Then click the value, type 4, and click "set".
steps.why: Its lamp lights once the beaker is clearly acid.

steps.title: And a tenth again
steps.text: Pick up the second beaker, then right-click the third. Slide to 5 mL and pour. Watch the monitor's lamp.
steps.why: A thousandth of the bottle's acid: about pH 3. Still a thousand times more hydrogen ions than pure water has.

checks.text: the third beaker's pH between 2.4 and 3.5

fails.text: Acid went into the wrong beaker: the steps are a tenth each. Press reset to start again.

goal.text: every element, mass and energy unchanged
